opening.text: Imagine crossing a wide river on stepping stones. You can't jump the whole way. But if you step on each stone, one at a time, you reach the other side. Ordinances are like those stones. Baptism. The gift of the Holy Ghost. The temple. Each one is a step. Each one carries us closer to God.

mainMessage.text: Ordinances are sacred steps that take us across to God. Each one comes with a promise.

blocks.text: **Light on the path** Ordinances bring light into our lives. That is one of the big reasons to receive them.
But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light:
Elder Taniela B. Wakolo of the Seventy said this in his talk “Saving Ordinances Will Bring Us Marvelous Light” from the April 2018 general conference.
Today I want to focus on saving ordinances, which will bring you and me marvelous light.
Each step brings more light.
**Every stone has a promise** Each ordinance comes with a covenant. When we step on a stone, we make a promise to God.

Wherefore, do the things which I have told you I have seen that your Lord and your Redeemer should do; for, for this cause have they been shown unto me, that ye might know the gate by which ye should enter. For the gate by which ye should enter is repentance and baptism by water; and then cometh a remission of your sins by fire and by the Holy Ghost.
Elder Taniela B. Wakolo of the Seventy said this in his talk “Saving Ordinances Will Bring Us Marvelous Light” from the April 2018 general conference.
Like a coin with two sides, all the saving ordinances are accompanied by covenants with God.
Two sides, one coin.
**God keeps His side** When we honor our promises, God honors His. We can count on that.

And moreover, I would desire that ye should consider on the blessed and happy state of those that keep the commandments of God. For behold, they are blessed in all things, both temporal and spiritual; and if they hold out faithful to the end they are received into heaven, that thereby they may dwell with God in a state of never-ending happiness. O remember, remember that these things are true; for the Lord God hath spoken it.
Elder Taniela B. Wakolo of the Seventy said this in his talk “Saving Ordinances Will Bring Us Marvelous Light” from the April 2018 general conference.
God promised us blessings if we faithfully honor those covenants.
The promise is sure.
**Power in the stones** The stones are not just tradition. Real power comes through them.

Therefore, in the ordinances thereof, the power of godliness is manifest. And without the ordinances thereof, and the authority of the priesthood, the power of godliness is not manifest unto men in the flesh;
Elder Kent F. Richards of the Seventy said this in his talk “The Power of Godliness” from the April 2016 general conference.
These powers become available personally to each one of us through the ordinances and the covenants of the temple.
The power is real.
**The last stones are in the temple** The temple is where we step onto the highest stones. It is God's house, and there we can learn about His power.

And that all people who shall enter upon the threshold of the Lord’s house may feel thy power, and feel constrained to acknowledge that thou hast sanctified it, and that it is thy house, a place of thy holiness.
Elder Kent F. Richards of the Seventy said this in his talk “The Power of Godliness” from the April 2016 general conference.
Each temple is God’s holy, sacred house, and therein each of us may learn and know the powers of godliness.
The highest stones are there.
**You can't skip the stones** We can't jump the river. Jesus taught that we need to be born of water and of the Spirit. The path goes through the stones.
Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Let This House Be Built unto My Name” from the April 2020 general conference.
The most sacred covenants and priesthood ordinances are received only in a temple—the house of the Lord.
The path is the way across.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they received an ordinance and felt something real. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Jesus is baptized

blocks.text: Jesus had no sin. But He still came to be baptized.

Then cometh Jesus from Galilee to Jordan unto John, to be baptized of him. But John forbad him, saying, I have need to be baptized of thee, and comest thou to me? And Jesus answering said unto him, Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness. Then he suffered him.
If the Savior stepped on this stone, so can we. He showed us the way, and He walked it first.

application.text: First, think about which ordinances you have received. Second, remember the promises that came with each one. Third, choose one promise to live better this week.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know ordinances are real and sacred. I know God keeps His promises. I know Jesus Christ went first and shows us the way. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A lamp can sit on a table all day, and it gives no light until it's plugged in. The lamp is fine. The power is there. But the connection is what makes it shine. Ordinances are like that plug. They connect us to the power of God.

mainMessage.text: Ordinances connect us to God's power. Without the connection, the light does not come on.

blocks.text: **Light comes on** When we are connected, light comes into our lives. That is what ordinances bring.
But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light:
Elder Taniela B. Wakolo of the Seventy said this in his talk “Saving Ordinances Will Bring Us Marvelous Light” from the April 2018 general conference.
Today I want to focus on saving ordinances, which will bring you and me marvelous light.
The light comes on.
**A two-way connection** A plug has two prongs. An ordinance has two parts: what God gives and what we promise.

Wherefore, do the things which I have told you I have seen that your Lord and your Redeemer should do; for, for this cause have they been shown unto me, that ye might know the gate by which ye should enter. For the gate by which ye should enter is repentance and baptism by water; and then cometh a remission of your sins by fire and by the Holy Ghost.
Elder Taniela B. Wakolo of the Seventy said this in his talk “Saving Ordinances Will Bring Us Marvelous Light” from the April 2018 general conference.
Like a coin with two sides, all the saving ordinances are accompanied by covenants with God.
Two parts, one connection.
**The power never runs out** A lamp stays lit as long as it stays plugged in. God's promises last as long as we stay faithful.

And moreover, I would desire that ye should consider on the blessed and happy state of those that keep the commandments of God. For behold, they are blessed in all things, both temporal and spiritual; and if they hold out faithful to the end they are received into heaven, that thereby they may dwell with God in a state of never-ending happiness. O remember, remember that these things are true; for the Lord God hath spoken it.
Elder Taniela B. Wakolo of the Seventy said this in his talk “Saving Ordinances Will Bring Us Marvelous Light” from the April 2018 general conference.
God promised us blessings if we faithfully honor those covenants.
Stay connected.
**Real current** This is not a symbol with nothing behind it. Real power flows when ordinances are received and covenants kept.

Therefore, in the ordinances thereof, the power of godliness is manifest. And without the ordinances thereof, and the authority of the priesthood, the power of godliness is not manifest unto men in the flesh;
Elder Kent F. Richards of the Seventy said this in his talk “The Power of Godliness” from the April 2016 general conference.
These powers become available personally to each one of us through the ordinances and the covenants of the temple.
The current is real.
**The main power source** The temple is where we connect most fully. In God's house, we can learn about His power and feel it.

And that all people who shall enter upon the threshold of the Lord’s house may feel thy power, and feel constrained to acknowledge that thou hast sanctified it, and that it is thy house, a place of thy holiness.
Elder Kent F. Richards of the Seventy said this in his talk “The Power of Godliness” from the April 2016 general conference.
Each temple is God’s holy, sacred house, and therein each of us may learn and know the powers of godliness.
The main source is there.
**Only one outlet** The Lord set one way to receive the highest blessings. We follow His pattern.
Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Let This House Be Built unto My Name” from the April 2020 general conference.
The most sacred covenants and priesthood ordinances are received only in a temple—the house of the Lord.
His way is the way.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they took the sacrament and felt connected to Christ. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The first sacrament

blocks.text: On the night before His death, Jesus gathered His apostles. He gave them something simple to remember Him by.

And he took bread, and gave thanks, and brake it, and gave unto them, saying, This is my body which is given for you: this do in remembrance of me. Likewise also the cup after supper, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood, which is shed for you.
The sacrament is an ordinance we can receive every week. It plugs us back in.

application.text: First, decide to prepare for the sacrament this Sunday. Second, think about one promise you will renew. Third, listen closely to the prayers.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know ordinances bring us the power of God. I know the sacrament renews us. I know Jesus Christ is the source of all light. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

mainMessage.text: Ordinances are gates on the path home. Each one opens the way to more light.

Today I want to focus on saving ordinances, which will bring you and me marvelous light.
The gate leads to light.
**The latch is a promise** To open a gate, you work the latch. To receive an ordinance, we make a covenant.

Elder Taniela B. Wakolo of the Seventy said this in his talk “Saving Ordinances Will Bring Us Marvelous Light” from the April 2018 general conference.
Like a coin with two sides, all the saving ordinances are accompanied by covenants with God.

Elder Taniela B. Wakolo of the Seventy said this in his talk “Saving Ordinances Will Bring Us Marvelous Light” from the April 2018 general conference.
God promised us blessings if we faithfully honor those covenants.
Blessings wait ahead.
**The gate opens to power** Walking through brings us real strength from God.

Therefore, in the ordinances thereof, the power of godliness is manifest. And without the ordinances thereof, and the authority of the priesthood, the power of godliness is not manifest unto men in the flesh;
Elder Kent F. Richards of the Seventy said this in his talk “The Power of Godliness” from the April 2016 general conference.
These powers become available personally to each one of us through the ordinances and the covenants of the temple.
Strength is on the other side.
**The final gate** The temple is the gate to the highest blessings. In God's house, we learn how great His power is.

And that all people who shall enter upon the threshold of the Lord’s house may feel thy power, and feel constrained to acknowledge that thou hast sanctified it, and that it is thy house, a place of thy holiness.
Elder Kent F. Richards of the Seventy said this in his talk “The Power of Godliness” from the April 2016 general conference.
Each temple is God’s holy, sacred house, and therein each of us may learn and know the powers of godliness.
The last gate is holy.
**No way around** We can't climb the fence and skip the gate. The Lord has asked us to come in through His door.
Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Let This House Be Built unto My Name” from the April 2020 general conference.
The most sacred covenants and priesthood ordinances are received only in a temple—the house of the Lord.
We go through the gate.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they said yes to an invitation to make a covenant. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The Ethiopian is baptized

blocks.text: An Ethiopian official was reading the scriptures when Philip joined him. When they came to some water, he asked a simple question.

And as they went on their way, they came unto a certain water: and the eunuch said, See, here is water; what doth hinder me to be baptized? And Philip said, If thou believest with all thine heart, thou mayest. And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God. And he commanded the chariot to stand still: and they went down both into the water, both Philip and the eunuch; and he baptized him. And when they were come up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, that the eunuch saw him no more: and he went on his way rejoicing.
He didn't wait. He went through the gate. And he went on his way rejoicing. That is what the gate gives us.

application.text: First, think about a gate you are ready to walk through, like a baptism, a temple visit or a renewed promise. Second, talk to someone who can help you take the step. Third, set a date.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know ordinances open the way to God. I know the joy that comes after. I know Jesus Christ is the keeper of the gate. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A locked door has one right key. You can try a hundred others. None will work. But when you find the right one, the door swings open with no effort. God has given us keys to open the door to eternal life. The keys are ordinances, given by His authority.

mainMessage.text: Ordinances are the keys God gave us to open the door to His greatest blessings.

blocks.text: **The door opens to light** What is behind the door is wonderful. It is the light of God.
But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light:
Elder Taniela B. Wakolo of the Seventy said this in his talk “Saving Ordinances Will Bring Us Marvelous Light” from the April 2018 general conference.
Today I want to focus on saving ordinances, which will bring you and me marvelous light.
The key opens to light.
**The key has two edges** A key is cut on both sides to fit. An ordinance has two sides too: God's gift and our promise.

Wherefore, do the things which I have told you I have seen that your Lord and your Redeemer should do; for, for this cause have they been shown unto me, that ye might know the gate by which ye should enter. For the gate by which ye should enter is repentance and baptism by water; and then cometh a remission of your sins by fire and by the Holy Ghost.
Elder Taniela B. Wakolo of the Seventy said this in his talk “Saving Ordinances Will Bring Us Marvelous Light” from the April 2018 general conference.
Like a coin with two sides, all the saving ordinances are accompanied by covenants with God.
Two sides fit the lock.
**Keep the key safe** A key does no good if we lose it. We keep our covenants, and God keeps His promises.

And moreover, I would desire that ye should consider on the blessed and happy state of those that keep the commandments of God. For behold, they are blessed in all things, both temporal and spiritual; and if they hold out faithful to the end they are received into heaven, that thereby they may dwell with God in a state of never-ending happiness. O remember, remember that these things are true; for the Lord God hath spoken it.
Elder Taniela B. Wakolo of the Seventy said this in his talk “Saving Ordinances Will Bring Us Marvelous Light” from the April 2018 general conference.
God promised us blessings if we faithfully honor those covenants.
Keep it close.
**The key turns real power** The lock is real, and so is the power that follows when the door opens.

Therefore, in the ordinances thereof, the power of godliness is manifest. And without the ordinances thereof, and the authority of the priesthood, the power of godliness is not manifest unto men in the flesh;
Elder Kent F. Richards of the Seventy said this in his talk “The Power of Godliness” from the April 2016 general conference.
These powers become available personally to each one of us through the ordinances and the covenants of the temple.
The power is behind the door.
**The master door** The temple is where the most important doors open. It is God's house, and we can learn of Him there.

And that all people who shall enter upon the threshold of the Lord’s house may feel thy power, and feel constrained to acknowledge that thou hast sanctified it, and that it is thy house, a place of thy holiness.
Elder Kent F. Richards of the Seventy said this in his talk “The Power of Godliness” from the April 2016 general conference.
Each temple is God’s holy, sacred house, and therein each of us may learn and know the powers of godliness.
The master doors are there.
**One lock, one key** The Lord decided how the door opens. We don't have to guess. He told us.
Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Let This House Be Built unto My Name” from the April 2020 general conference.
The most sacred covenants and priesthood ordinances are received only in a temple—the house of the Lord.
He told us the way.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they asked what they needed to do to follow God. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: What shall we do?

blocks.text: Peter had just taught a crowd about Jesus. They were moved to the heart. They asked a direct question.

Now when they heard this, they were pricked in their heart, and said unto Peter and to the rest of the apostles, Men and brethren, what shall we do? Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.
Their question was honest, and the answer was clear. God makes the path plain for those who ask.

application.text: First, ask God in prayer, "What should I do next?" Second, write down what you feel. Third, act on it this week.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God has given us the keys to eternal life. I know He answers when we ask. I know Jesus Christ opens the door. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A ladder doesn't ask you to climb it all at once. You put your hand on one rung and your foot on the next. Rung by rung, you rise. Ordinances are like that ladder. Baptism is a rung. The sacrament is a rung. The temple is a rung. Each one lifts us a little higher toward God.

mainMessage.text: Ordinances are rungs on a ladder that lifts us toward God. We take them one at a time.

blocks.text: **Higher means lighter** The higher we climb, the more light we see. That is the gift of each ordinance.
But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light:
Elder Taniela B. Wakolo of the Seventy said this in his talk “Saving Ordinances Will Bring Us Marvelous Light” from the April 2018 general conference.
Today I want to focus on saving ordinances, which will bring you and me marvelous light.
Each rung lifts us toward light.
**Grip and step** A climber needs a grip and a step. An ordinance gives us both: what God offers and what we promise.

Wherefore, do the things which I have told you I have seen that your Lord and your Redeemer should do; for, for this cause have they been shown unto me, that ye might know the gate by which ye should enter. For the gate by which ye should enter is repentance and baptism by water; and then cometh a remission of your sins by fire and by the Holy Ghost.
Elder Taniela B. Wakolo of the Seventy said this in his talk “Saving Ordinances Will Bring Us Marvelous Light” from the April 2018 general conference.
Like a coin with two sides, all the saving ordinances are accompanied by covenants with God.
Hand and foot, promise and gift.
**The ladder is held** Someone is holding the base. God keeps His promises to those who keep theirs.

And moreover, I would desire that ye should consider on the blessed and happy state of those that keep the commandments of God. For behold, they are blessed in all things, both temporal and spiritual; and if they hold out faithful to the end they are received into heaven, that thereby they may dwell with God in a state of never-ending happiness. O remember, remember that these things are true; for the Lord God hath spoken it.
Elder Taniela B. Wakolo of the Seventy said this in his talk “Saving Ordinances Will Bring Us Marvelous Light” from the April 2018 general conference.
God promised us blessings if we faithfully honor those covenants.
He holds the ladder.
**The ladder is solid** This ladder is not a drawing. It is real, and it bears our weight. Real power comes through each rung.

Therefore, in the ordinances thereof, the power of godliness is manifest. And without the ordinances thereof, and the authority of the priesthood, the power of godliness is not manifest unto men in the flesh;
Elder Kent F. Richards of the Seventy said this in his talk “The Power of Godliness” from the April 2016 general conference.
These powers become available personally to each one of us through the ordinances and the covenants of the temple.
It holds our weight.
**The top rungs** The temple is where we reach the top rungs. In God's house, we learn of His power.

And that all people who shall enter upon the threshold of the Lord’s house may feel thy power, and feel constrained to acknowledge that thou hast sanctified it, and that it is thy house, a place of thy holiness.
Elder Kent F. Richards of the Seventy said this in his talk “The Power of Godliness” from the April 2016 general conference.
Each temple is God’s holy, sacred house, and therein each of us may learn and know the powers of godliness.
The top rungs are holy.
**No rung can be skipped** We can't leap to the top. Jesus taught that we must be born of water and of the Spirit. We climb in order.
Jesus answered, Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Let This House Be Built unto My Name” from the April 2020 general conference.
The most sacred covenants and priesthood ordinances are received only in a temple—the house of the Lord.
We climb one rung at a time.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they or someone close to them took a step of faith toward an ordinance. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Cornelius and his household

blocks.text: Cornelius was a good man who had never heard the full gospel. When Peter taught him, the Holy Ghost came upon his household. Peter then asked a question.

Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, which have received the Holy Ghost as well as we? And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord. Then prayed they him to tarry certain days.
They were ready, and Peter did not make them wait. When our hearts are ready, the next rung is there.

application.text: First, think about your next rung. It might be baptism, renewing covenants at the sacrament or going to the temple. Second, talk to someone who can help you get ready. Third, take the step.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know ordinances lift us to God. I know the power is real. I know Jesus Christ holds the ladder and walks beside us. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
